findings.current: if I kill enough of them
findings.defect: “Enough” adds a quantity or threshold. 닥치는 대로 쳐 죽이면 means killing them indiscriminately or as they come, not killing a sufficient number.
findings.rationale: The speaker boasts that he will kill Dark Heaven members indiscriminately, make a name for himself, and earn money; the Korean does not specify how many he must kill.
findings.replacement: if I kill them as they come

findings.current: Hong Jeok, Red Turbans, whatever you call yourself
findings.defect: This makes “Red Turbans” sound like another name the visitor uses for himself. The Korean contrasts Hong Jeok with the Red Turban bandits, not two possible names for the visitor.
findings.rationale: The guard dismissively says that whether the visitor is Hong Jeok or a Red Turban, he still has to undergo verification.
findings.replacement: Hong Jeok, Red Turbans, whatever—you still have to go through verification

findings.current: “Spatula Chin! That chin takes my breath away! Chin-chin, ka-thunk-thunk-chin!”
findings.defect: The source repeats “Spatula Chin!” twice before the next phrase. The English drops one repetition, weakening the deliberately escalating chant.
findings.rationale: The Korean explicitly repeats 주걱턱 twice as part of the taunting chant.
findings.replacement: “Spatula Chin! Spatula Chin! That chin takes my breath away! Chin-chin, ka-thunk-thunk-chin!”

findings.current: departed with a spear on his back instead of a fishing rod
findings.defect: The translation omits the suddenness of his departure.
findings.rationale: 홀연히 떠났다 describes the old man leaving suddenly; the accepted baseline also preserved that detail.
findings.replacement: abruptly departed with a spear on his back instead of a fishing rod

summary: The chapter is largely faithful, but a few lines add or alter source details and one comic beat loses an explicit repetition.
